answer: Sybil resistance follows from EigenTrust’s reciprocity-weighted transitivity: reputation gains influence only through trusted peers and verified service. An exponential temporal half-life steadily erodes stale scores, so an identity must provide sustained honest work to remain an anchor in the trust graph. A freshly spawned sybil begins with near-zero eigenvector centrality; without reciprocal trust paths, its pulse cannot propagate, and it cannot cross the consensus threshold. Cloned identities thus cannot instantly grow a vine of credible reputation.
